score_notes.novelty: The idea of using the browser's storage quota as a reserved-but-unused void is genuinely fresh — the catalogue treats absence extensively (Inert Gas, Unreachable, Zone de Sensibilité) but never as a measured, to-scale bar of bytes the platform itself has set aside for you.
score_notes.nuance: Mechanism and concept collapse cleanly (P1): the bar IS the API report, the 'use nothing' ethic IS the medium, and Klein's void is relocated rather than illustrated; the verdict copy and re-measure button land the literate reading without requiring wall text, though the footer prose borders on explaining the joke.
score_notes.narrative: Sits squarely on the dematerialization / value axis (P6) and answers Klein directly while echoing Barry's gallery-closure and Benjamin's aura — a named prior work, legibly placed, though it does not extend the twenty-year argument with a genuinely new move beyond the found-object itself.
score_notes.craft: One API call, one bar, one plate, one button — the build is nearly the smallest possible, with clean typography and a honest hairline fallback when usage > 0; the verdict copy is the only fat, and even it is small.
score_notes.wit: The dry joke — 'gigabytes reserved, zero used' — lands immediately and again on re-reading as Klein's whitewashed room; not quite as self-cancelling as 'But is it art?' but tonally exact.

references_named: Yves Klein, Le Vide (Galerie Iris Clert, 1958)
Robert Barry, During the exhibition the gallery will be closed (1969)
Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
rationale: Le Vide (Reserved, Unused) finds a genuinely fresh web-native found object — the StorageManager quota — and turns Klein's dematerialized gallery into a measurable, falsifiable bar drawn from the platform's own bookkeeping. The mechanism enacts the idea (P1) and the delivery ethic (P8) becomes the artwork itself. It is materially distinct from the catalogue: no prior work uses storage estimation as material, and it relocates the void lineage (Klein, Barry, Klein's receipt-burning) onto disk space. The narrative ties to Klein and Barry cleanly but does not push the twenty-year arc further than those names already did, and the verdict copy leans slightly toward wall-text rather than pure double-coding.
reservations: The footer paragraph and verdict line explain the joke a touch too explicitly for full P7 restraint — the casual viewer is told what to read, rather than being left to encounter Klein themselves.
revision_suggestion: Strip the explanatory footer paragraph (or cut it to one line of attribution + license) and let the bar, the plate, and Klein's name do the work; the re-measure button can stay as the only interactive gesture.
